subject: Finlytics demo: model shortlist and deployment priorities
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Anna Lowe <anna@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Finlytics demo: model shortlist and deployment priorities

Hi Anna —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick demo recap + my proposed next steps so we can make the shortlist actionable for your engineering and procurement teams.

High-level recommendation (shortlist):
- Redwood-Base-13B-q4: Low cost, good for high-throughput API use; strong latency profile for short responses.
- OpenDialogue-40B-fp16: Higher quality on long-form analysis (better factuality on long contexts) but higher compute cost.
- InstructLite-7B-pt: Cheap baseline for prompt routing / safety classification tasks.

Attached Ive included the initial benchmark CSV and the prompt set we used in the demo. Links below:
- Benchmark summary (CSV attached)
- Prompt set v1 (attached)
- Full eval/runbook matrix: Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/finlytics-eval

Key tradeoffs we discussed: cost vs. latency vs. long-context quality
- If Finlytics prioritizes sub-250ms p95 for UI flows, Redwood-Base-13B-q4 is the best fit.
- If accuracy on long financial reports (8k+ tokens) is the top priority, plan to eval OpenDialogue-40B-fp16 or a dedicated RAG pipeline.

Proposed next steps (can overlap):
1) Permission to run a 48–72h expanded eval on your sample dataset (well ingest ~2k representative docs).
2) Well produce a focused benchmark measuring p50/p95 latency, cost per 1M tokens, and hallucination rate on your test set.
3) Quick pricing sketch for Hosted vs. Dedicated for the shortlisted models (well include reserved capacity numbers if you plan sustained load).
4) Align on security items procurement will need (SOC2, IP terms) — Ill loop in our security lead if needed.

Action: Can you confirm if procurement should be CCd on the evaluation scope and whether there are any disallowed external datasets or IP constraints? Also, what SLO (p95) is your internal target for interactive features?

Attachments: finlytics_benchmarks_v1.csv (csv), finlytics_prompt_set_v1.md (md), runbook_eval_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

Thanks —
Mina Haddad
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mina@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0193

From: Anna Lowe <anna@finlytics.com>

Subject: Re: Finlytics demo: model shortlist and deployment priorities

Thanks, Mina — really clear summary and helpful shortlist. A few clarifying questions before we greenlight the expanded eval: 

1) For the p95 latency you quoted (sub-250ms for Redwood-Base-13B-q4) — is that measured on a single request at 512 tokens or with concurrent load (10–20 RPS)? Were trying to size a UI tier that sees bursts to 50 RPS.
2) Can you give a rough cost estimate (hosted) for 1M tokens for each of the three shortlisted models? If you can provide both hosted and a ballpark for dedicated nightly reserved capacity thatd be ideal.
3) About long-document fidelity: do you have a recommended RAG setup or chunking strategy for the 8k+ reports we showed? Any sample prompt engineering guidelines would help.
4) Procurement will want SOC 2 and basic data handling docs. Can you attach or point me to those?

Once we have those answers we can confirm scope and loop in procurement. Also happy to schedule a 30-min call with your product/ops folks to finalize the eval matrix.

Thanks —
Anna
Anna Lowe | Head of Product, Finlytics
anna@finlytics.com

Mina / Marissa — quick internal note on prioritization if we get the greenlight for the 48–72h eval: 

Eval priority order (fast -> deeper):
1) Redwood-Base-13B-q4 (baseline): measure p50/p95 at 1, 10, 50 concurrent RPS; capture CPU/GPU utilization and token cost.
2) InstructLite-7B-pt (cheap classifier/routing baseline): measure accuracy on safety / classification prompts and cost as a fallback.
3) OpenDialogue-40B-fp16 (long-context quality): run targeted long-report QA and hallucination F1; include RAG variants.

Suggested metrics to capture per run: p50, p95, cold-start latency (first token), tokenized cost, hallucination rate (manual sample), and top-K response diversity.

Quick config notes: for the concurrent load test run we should use batching window: 12–20ms and enable KV cache warmup steps for the long-context runs. For p95 numbers at 50 RPS, we may need dedicated pools or burst policies — we should outline Dedicated pricing as part of the follow-up.

Ill prepare a short script to collect these metrics and attach to the Drive eval folder if Mina approves.

—Karthik

Hi Anna — quick answers inline and next steps.

On Mon, May 2, 2027 at 12:47 PM Anna Lowe <anna@finlytics.com> wrote:
> 1) For the p95 latency you quoted (sub-250ms for Redwood-Base-13B-q4) — is that measured on a single request at 512 tokens or with concurrent load (10–20 RPS)?

That number is our baseline measured at 1–5 RPS with a 512 token prompt on g4dn-like hardware (no batching). Under moderate batching (12–20ms window) and 10 RPS you should expect p95 in the ~300–350ms range. At sustained 50 RPS we recommend Dedicated pools; I can include Dedicated sketches in the pricing note.

> 2) Can you give a rough cost estimate (hosted) for 1M tokens for each of the three shortlisted models?

Rough hosted estimates (ballpark):
- Redwood-Base-13B-q4: ~$0.75–$1.10 per 1M tokens (depends on prompt/response ratio).
- InstructLite-7B-pt: ~$0.20–$0.35 per 1M tokens.
- OpenDialogue-40B-fp16: ~$3.50–$5.00 per 1M tokens.

Dedicated nightly reserved (very approximate): per-GPU equivalent lowers unit cost ~25–40% depending on commit level; Ill produce a short matrix once you confirm expected token volumes.

> 3) About long-document fidelity: do you have a recommended RAG setup or chunking strategy for the 8k+ reports we showed?

Yes — recommended approach for Finlytics:
- Chunking: 1k token overlapping windows (200 token overlap) and semantic index by paragraph embeddings.
- Retriever: sparse + ANN hybrid (embedding-based re-ranker) to keep retrieval recall high.
- Prompt template: explicit instruction + source attribution block to reduce hallucination. I attached a sample prompt in finlytics_prompt_set_v1.md.

> 4) Procurement will want SOC 2 and basic data handling docs. Can you attach or point me to those?

Attached: short SOC 2 summary is in our security portal (link below). If procurement needs full artifacts well have our security contact submit the package under NDA.
